problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-3x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector corresponding to the only eigenvalue of the system's matrix $A$ is $v=[1,\text{ }0]^{T}.$ The vector $w=[0,\text{ }1]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]{{field-1}}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-3t}{{field-2}},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$
